recipes.name: Healthier Chicken Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Cook chicken in a nonstick skillet over medium heat until no longer pink and juices run clear, about 10 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of breasts should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

Drain excess fat. Cube chicken and return to skillet. Add onion, sour cream, 1 cup Cheddar cheese, parsley, oregano, and black pepper. Heat until cheese melts, about 3 minutes. Stir in salt, tomato sauce, water, chili powder, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, garlic, and black beans.
Roll even amounts of chicken mixture into tortillas. Arrange in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Cover with taco sauce and 3/4 cup Cheddar cheese.
Bake uncovered in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and sauce is bubbling, about 20 minutes. Cool 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Chicken Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: A family favorite, these healthy chicken enchiladas are made with reduced-fat cheese, beans, bell peppers, and whole wheat tortillas. Colorful and flavorful!

review.reviewBody: I used FF plain yogurt instead of the sour cream and corn tortillas just because I prefer them. I also threw my peppers and onion in the pan and sauteed them slightly, but they were still crunchy, which I like. I also did not roll the tortillas but made them into a layered casserole. I love the addition of red bell pepper and black beans to this healthier version. I enjoyed this dish and would definitely make it again.

These enchiladas turned out great. As written, it is probably very good, but I did make some minor adjustments to suit my taste buds. Prior to cooking the chicken, I used a tablespoon of vegetable oil in the skillet and seasoned the chicken breasts with Cajun seasoning (a small dusting of taco seasoning would work here also). After removing the chicken from the skillet, I added another tablespoon of vegetable oil and sauteed the onion in the same skillet. When the onion was translucent I added one poblano pepper (in lieu of the bell peppers) to the skillet and sauteed until softened. I added the water at this point so that it could incorporate all the bits in the skillet. Then I added the chicken. I substituted fresh cilantro for the parsley. From there, I followed the recipe except I used nonfat plain Greek yogurt instead of the sour cream and added a teaspoon of cumin with the chili powder. I also added whole kernel corn with the black beans. Before serving, I topped them with nonfat plain Greek yogurt and fresh cilantro. I served them with a side of fat free refried beans and Spanish rice. My hubby loved it! Now I have an awesome chicken enchilada recipe that I can work into my Weight Watchers program. Whoo-hoo! :)

I really like this recipe as a base recipe, I changed the red sauce to green chili sauce, and I used fat free cheddar cheese, cottage cheese and sour cream, also low carb whole wheat tortillas. I baked my chicken breasts for an hour then put my chopped red onion , green and red bell pepper in with the chicken for 20 mins. after that all cooked, I mixed my cottage cheese, fat free cheddar cheese, 1 package of green chili enchilada sauce and sour cream in with my chopped up chicken breasts. I spooned my enchilada mixture into my tortillas and rolled them up in rows in my baking pan. then I poured my other package of green chili sauce on top of the rolled up tortillas and then sprinkled a package of fat free cheddar cheese on top. I baked it on 350 for 35 min. turned out better than I could have imagined.

I've made this 3 times, and my family loves it. I like the fact that it doesn't use canned soup for the base. Instead of chopping up two different colors of bell peppers, I just use red. I have found that I need to use two 9 x 13 inch baking pans to fit all 8 tortillas without crowding them. After examining the nutrition labels on the tortilla bags, I found that the "Carb Balance" variety from Mission is excellent. If you don't have shredded reduced fat cheddar cheese, then shredded reduced fat cheddar jack works just as well. For the chicken breast, I have used a $4.99 rotisserie chicken from Costco, and it was very easy to get all the meat off it after it got very cold in the refrigerator. Chopping up the onion and bell pepper at the start of the week and keeping them in airtight containers in the produce drawer of the fridge is a real time saver. I am going to pre-measure the parsley, oregano, black pepper, and chili powder and keep them in small zip-lock bags to make meal prep faster. For the 12 ounce jar of taco sauce, try a variety of products to find the one that has the desired thickness for you and your family because some products are much thinner than others. Whole Foods has a very good jarred enchilada sauce. Thank you very much for such a terrific recipe, MakeItHealthy!

I made several modifications to this based on what I had - we also love spicy food so I add kick to everything. I halved and butterflied two giant chicken breasts, added S&P, cooked on a grill pan and minced the chicken. I pre-cooked the onion and peppers before adding anything else (about double the peppers), and used diced hot cherry pepper instead of red (just one). I used fat-free yogurt in place of sour cream, added a can of diced tomatoes instead of sauce, added 1/4 salsa, and added 2 tsp. cumin, 1/4 cup taco seasoning and exchanged cilantro for oregano, and used white beans instead of black. As with any dish like this I cooked the filling for about 20 minutes. I used whole wheat tortillas and only used enough taco sauce to cover the enchiladas (maybe 1/3 cup). I only had 4 tortillas, so the rest of the filling is...dare I say, delicious chicken chili??

I will make this many more times!! It's healthy, fairly cheap and easy to make. I made yellow rice to go with the enchiladas, so you could potentially and comfortably feed eight people. I made a few minor adjustments. I used a jar of chunky salsa in place of the water, tomato sauce, onion and peppers. I also added a half teaspoon of ground cumin and a sprinkle of cayenne pepper for a little heat. I used about one cup of stuffing per tortilla. It was a little difficult to roll, so I used a scrapper to help keep the stuffing in place while I rolled the tortilla over with my other hand. My very picky boyfriend enjoyed these so much that he went back for seconds!!

This recipe is great!! The low fat cheddar works fine in this recipe. 

The changes I made due to taste preferences were:

Greek Yogurt instead of sour cream. 
Used shredded chicken thighs with the breast as we had lots of let over CT from a cook out. 

One large can of black olives, sliced. Some mixed into the stuffing mix, some on top for visual delight. 

Made two pans of this, one pan got a can of green enchilada sauce on top, the other red. Sliced peppers on both. 

Daughter loved it, SIL loved it, I loved it. Ate on it the next day as we packed and helped them move. Also made some Spanish Rice with Jasmine variety rice. Good stuff.

I used Greek plain yogurt in place of sour cream. No tomato sauce or water. Grilled the chicken breast with taco seasoning on them. Once cooled I shredded them. Also used a can of green chilies and green enchilada sauce. Put everything but chicken in a pan and heated until well blended. Then took my soft shells, put chicken and spooned mixture on top followed by cheese. Roll up and continue until all shells are full. Pour remaining mixture over all enchiladas and a bit more cheese. I also used fresh cilantro instead of parsley. Absolutely wonderful dinner, making again today :)
Very tasty. I added chopped cilantro & tomoatos on the top for extra flavor & color.
Very good recipe, I shredded the chicken, used cumin instead of the oregano. It took 2 pans to fit all of the tortillas. Took about 30 mins to bake.

The taste was Great, but mine came out Sooooo runny. I followed directions to a T. i tried throwing n a little corn starch to thicken it up, but it wasn't enough & I didn't want to add anymore n fear of ruining the taste. I let it simmer & simmer forever, NJT Still no luck. I saw another review that said she had the same problem & refrigerated it. I guess we'll eat it tomorrow. 5 stars on taste, but 3 stars for the runniness. Next time I'll add less water. I even had extra chicken n it. Was Too runny to make enchiladas, so making burritos.
Heavier hand with the chili powder and garlic! Nice dish
Delicious! Had seconds AND leftovers

I’m actually a terrible cook so my family didn’t expect much out of this attempt, but loved it. It was a lot more prep than I thought, but it was worth it. I think next time, I’ll use shredded chicken, and that might be the only thing I’d change. Great recipe!!!

This was so easy to make and it was so delicious. Between my husband and I, we almost finished half of the dish... forced ourselves to stop. So yummy. Tips: make sure you have a large skillet to add all ingredients to during stove steps (I maxed mine out). If you like a crispy or browned cheese, broiled for 2-3 minutes before removing from the oven.
This turned out great. I did add a can of Rotel (we like it hot) for the pasta sauce and more cheese on top (can never go wrong with extra cheese)
We love, love love, this! We use Greek Yogurt in place of sour cream to make it even healthier. YUM!
This was good and easy to make. The only thing I would change is baking it a bit longer, the enchiladas were not very warm.

Made as directed and thought the flavor was delicious but the tortillas were grossly soggy. 
Scooped them out and used the filling and added a little corn to the mix and used it on chips with salsa and sour cream and shredded cheese on top and it made great nachos!!
Added Emerils SW Seasoning when cooking the chicken and will make again.
